comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C32-C40, C58-C60. Both evaluations find strong support for Numb's role in contractile force generation, with the double knockout experiments demonstrating that Numb loss drives the phenotype. All three peer reviewers affirm this as a convincing finding, matching OpenEval's assessment of well-supported claims with appropriate statistical analyses.

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C45. Both evaluations support the splice variant characterization showing absence of exon 9 and predominance of transcripts lacking exon 3. OpenEval explicitly endorses the PCR analysis approach, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization through overall study approval without critique.

Perfect agreement on claim C41. Both evaluations support the finding that normalized frequency-tension relationships are preserved despite reduced absolute force. OpenEval explicitly analyzes this data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it without challenge as part of the physiological characterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C7 and C57. Both evaluations support the finding that Numb loss disrupts Septin 7 organization. The second peer reviewer explicitly confirms 'loss of Numb/Numblike in myofibers causes changes in Septin 7 subcellular localization,' matching OpenEval's assessment of clear microscopy evidence.

Perfect agreement on claim C78. Both evaluations classify this as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval notes the claim is 'explicitly speculative' and 'an untested hypothesis,' while peer reviewers do not comment on this specific aging prediction, consistent with recognizing it as untested extrapolation.

Strong agreement on claims C47-C50, C61-C62 regarding mass spectrometry identification of septin binding partners. Both evaluations support the proteomics findings. However, OpenEval notes that membrane localization (C46) is indirect, while peer reviewers call for additional investigation of interaction specificity. OpenEval includes C87 (silver stain validation) which peer reviewers address separately.

Agreement on claims C4, C51, C63 regarding Numb-Septin 7 interaction. Both evaluations support the biochemical interaction data from proteomics and co-IP validation. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple evidence lines, while the second peer reviewer acknowledges the interaction but notes that mechanistic details require further exploration.

Agreement on claims C54-C56 regarding differential spatial expression patterns. Both evaluations support the single-nucleus sequencing and confocal microscopy data. OpenEval explicitly endorses the spatial localization findings, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the localization data that supports functional interpretations.

Agreement on claims C6, C52-C53 regarding colocalization patterns. Both evaluations support the confocal microscopy showing Numb and Septin 7 localization. OpenEval addresses C65 (inferential interpretation of overlapping functions), while peer reviewers focus on the baseline localization without explicitly discussing functional implications.

Agreement on uncertain status of claims C8 and C79. Both evaluations recognize these as broad mechanistic conclusions extending beyond direct evidence. OpenEval notes the causal link remains inferential, while the second peer reviewer calls for additional investigation to demonstrate biological relevance and specificity of the interaction.

Agreement on uncertain status of claims C68-C70. Both evaluations recognize these as alternative mechanistic explanations that cannot be distinguished with current data. OpenEval notes authors appropriately acknowledge uncertainty, while peer reviewers' call for specificity mapping suggests these details remain unresolved.

Agreement on uncertain status of claims C66-C67. Both evaluations recognize these as explicitly speculative explanations for partial colocalization. OpenEval notes no experimental evidence is provided, while peer reviewers do not explicitly endorse or challenge these speculations, consistent with recognizing them as unresolved.

Agreement on claims C46 and C87 regarding technical aspects of the proteomics approach. Both evaluations support the methodology. OpenEval notes membrane localization (C46) is indirect based on detergent requirement, while the third peer reviewer acknowledges the 'straight-forward yet elegant design' of the immunoprecipitation approach.

Partial agreement on claims C82-C84 regarding GWAS/WGS associations. OpenEval supports the systematic database searches but notes unclear biological significance. The second peer reviewer acknowledges identification of multiple binding partners (which relates to the broader context) but treats these genetic associations as secondary findings.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1, C10, C11, C76, C77 as supported background claims from prior published work (Carey et al., 2007; De Gasperi et al., 2022). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than cited background.

OpenEval evaluates claims C2, C19-C25 as supported background claims from authors' prior work (De Gasperi et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not explicitly assess these foundational citations.

OpenEval evaluates claim C85 regarding parallel phenotype in Septin 7 knockout (Gönczi et al., 2022) as supported by citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this contextual finding strengthens the biological significance of the Numb-Septin 7 interaction.

OpenEval evaluates claims C80-C81 as supported concluding statements about novel insights into muscle biology and protein interactomes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these summary conclusions, though reviewers' overall acceptance implies agreement.

Peer reviewers evaluate claims C71-C75 regarding additional septin family members and their potential complex formation. The second reviewer notes this as 'an interesting area for further investigation.' No corresponding OpenEval result specifically groups these claims, though they relate to broader proteomics findings in R4 and R12.
